LESSON: GEOMETRICAL CONSTRUCTIONS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Geometry
Topic 4.1: Geometrical Constructions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Geometrical Constructions, part of Geometry in Grade 8 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we construct polygons? 2. Where do we use polygons in real-life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. construct parallel and perpendicular lines in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Geometrical Constructions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. divide a line proportionally in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Geometrical Constructions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. identify angle properties of polygons in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Geometrical Constructions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. construct regular polygons up to a hexagon in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Geometrical Constructions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. construct irregular polygons up to a hexagon in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Geometrical Constructions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. construct circles passing through the vertices of a

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Geometrical Constructions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. construct parallel and perpendicular lines in different situations,

   Geometrical Constructions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. divide a line proportionally in different situations,

   Geometrical Constructions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. identify angle properties of polygons in different situations,

   Geometrical Constructions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. construct regular polygons up to a hexagon in different situations,

   Geometrical Constructions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. construct irregular polygons up to a hexagon in different situations,

   Geometrical Constructions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. construct circles passing through the vertices of a

   Geometrical Constructions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

G. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. practice constructing parallel and perpendicular lines,

2. practice dividing a line proportionally, for example, using a set square and a ruler only or pair of compasses,

3. discuss angle properties of polygons and relate the number of right angles to the number of sides and determine the angles in a given polygon,

4. construct regular polygons using pair of compasses, rulers and protractors,

5. construct irregular polygons using pair of compasses, rulers and protractors. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. practice constructing parallel and perpendicular lines,
2. practice dividing a line proportionally, for example, using a set square and a ruler only or pair of compasses,
3. discuss angle properties of polygons and relate the number of right angles to the number of sides and determine the angles in a given polygon,
4. construct regular polygons using pair of compasses, rulers and protractors,
5. construct irregular polygons using pair of compasses, rulers and protractors. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Geometrical Constructions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: as the learner discusses angle properties of polygons and relate the number of right

angles to the number of sides.

• Digital literacy: as the learner uses IT devices or other resources to create patterns using circles touching sides of triangles

or polygons.

Values

Responsibility: as the learner constructs regular polygons using pair of compasses, rulers and protractors and take care of the
